(a) Inside the United States Projects.—The table in section 2101(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (division B of Public Law 109–364; 120 Stat. 2445), as amended by section 20814 of the Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2007 (division B of Public Law 109–289) and section 2105(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2008 (division B of Public Law 110–181; 122 Stat. 507), is further amended in the item relating to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, by striking “$96,900,000” in the amount column and inserting “$75,900,000”. 
    (b) Outside the United States Projects.—The table in section 2101(b) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (division B of Public Law 109–364; 120 Stat. 2446), as amended by section 2106(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2008 (division B of Public Law 110–181; 122 Stat. 508), is further amended in the item relating to Vicenza, Italy, by striking “$223,000,000” in the amount column and inserting “$208,280,000”. 
    (c) Conforming Amendments.—Section 2104(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (division B of Public Law 109–364; 120 Stat. 2447), as amended by section 2105(b) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2008 (division B of Public Law 110–181; 122 Stat. 508), is further amended—
        (1) in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking “$3,275,700,000” and inserting “$3,239,980,000”; 
        (2) in paragraph (1), by striking “$1,119,450,000” and inserting “$1,098,450,000”; and 
        (3) in paragraph (2), by striking “$510,582,00” and inserting “$495,862,000”.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts in military construction authorization tables for Fort Bragg and Vicenza, plus conforming changes to the authorization totals. There is no tempting participation reading: it provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to appropriation tables, specifically adjusting dollar amounts for military construction projects. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The actors involved are Congress (via the statute) and the executive branch (via the implementation of the appropriations), which are all inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The table in section 2101(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 ... is further amended in the item relating to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, by striking “$96,900,000” in the amount column and inserting “$75,900,000”.

opus.w: This section only changes authorized funding amounts for military construction projects at Fort Bragg and Vicenza and makes matching changes to the totals. It does not have the federal government consult or coordinate with anyone outside it, and it sets up no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. The formal amendment language is just how Congress changes a law; nobody outside the government takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of amendments to appropriation tables, adjusting dollar amounts for specific military construction projects. It does not contain any language requiring consultation, coordination, or input from state, local, tribal, or private entities. The actors involved are Congress and federal agencies (via the referenced Acts), which are inside the federal government. Therefore, there is no participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing funding amounts for military construction projects in Italy or North Carolina involves coordination with local governments or the public. However, the text itself only describes amendments to appropriation tables and does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties. It is purely a fiscal adjustment within the federal government.
